confirmed.title: Up & Down UP/DOWN buttons: a held Enter places a new bet on every auto-repeat, because the held-key rule exists only inside an open Modal
confirmed.scenario: A signed-in keyboard player is on /updown (a board card) or /updown/[roundId] with no side chosen and the TZS 1,000 chip selected. They Tab to UP and hold Enter for about 2 s. Keydown 1 clicks UP and places bet 1. After the OS repeat delay (about 0.5 s), every repeat keydown (about 30 a second) clicks UP again. Each time, bet.place('UP') runs with a fresh idempotency key, so bets 2, 3, 4 and on are placed with no confirm. Pending never disables the buttons. The burst ends only when the balance check (which counts in-flight spend) disables UP, or when the server's bet.place bucket (30, refilling 10 a minute) starts answering 'Slow down' with a sticky red toast for each refusal. That is up to about 30 real bets. On the round page the burst stops once bet 1's receipt takes focus, which takes as long as the network does (seconds on 2G). On the board it never stops (see updown-card-wrapper-starves-held-key-rule). There is a second way in: a held Enter, or a quick double Enter, on the receipt's 'Endelea kucheza' (Keep playing) closes the receipt. Modal then puts focus back on UP, and each remaining repeat, or the second press, places a bet. Space is not the risk on UP itself, because it clicks only once, on release.
confirmed.evidence: src/components/updown/updown-stake-controls.tsx:247-249 ('The buttons stay ENABLED - repeat taps are repeat bets'), :250-251 and :261-262 (onClick=guard(() => bet.place(...)); disabled only on !stakeReady || insufficient || locallyLocked, never on pending). src/components/updown/use-quick-bet.ts:163-164 ('do not debounce'); :302-336 (place() mints a new idempotency key on every call at :325-327, has no pending or in-flight gate, and starts the bet at :332); :245 (insufficient counts in-flight spend). src/lib/server/rate-limit.ts:97 (bet.place capacity 30, refillPerMin 10). The rule runs only from modal.tsx:291, inside the open-dialog effect (modal.tsx:273-315), even though held-key.ts:4-8 itself says the browser presses a focused button on every repeated Enter. Receipt path: updown-bet-receipt-modal.tsx:69 and :110-129 (primary = onClose, no onPrimary); operation-result-modal.tsx:387-394 (initialFocus=primaryRef) and :523; updown-stake-controls.tsx:347-357 (onClose=bet.clearPlacedReceipt); use-quick-bet.ts:260-261; modal.tsx:276-279 and :309-314 (focus returns to the element that had focus when the receipt opened, which is UP). The round page hosts the same controls (round-stake-panel.tsx:106). Its locked-side gold Confirm is disabled while pending (round-stake-panel.tsx:262-264), so that button is bounded by the round trip. Neither guard has an Up & Down case (scripts/enter-where-pressed.test.mts:32-37; scripts/qa-enter-where-pressed.mjs:11-20).
confirmed.proposedFix: Make an auto-repeat press nothing on money buttons outside dialogs. Export one noHeldRepeat handler from held-key.ts: an onKeyDown that calls preventDefault when e.repeat is true and the key is Enter or Space. Cancelling the repeated keydown cancels its keypress and click, which is A8i's own mechanism. Put it on UP and DOWN in updown-stake-controls.tsx and on round-stake-panel.tsx's gold Confirm. Alternatively, install the held-key rule once, app-wide, as a window CAPTURE listener (for example in AppShell). It would swallow any repeat=true Enter or Space that held-key.ts says would press something, whether a dialog is open or not. Deliberate taps (repeat=false) remain repeat bets, as Ali ruled. The hold-after-close in held-key-stops-at-close-reopens-confirm also closes the receipt path. The lenses split here: old-draft left a key held on 'Juu' itself to Ali's standing ruling and proposed only the hold after the receipt closes, while money-census, browser-semantics and regression read an auto-repeat as not a tap. Add a census check that money buttons outside dialogs carry the repeat guard. Add drive cases for Enter held on a board card's UP, and for Enter held or double-pressed on the receipt's primary. In each case the wallet must move by exactly one stake.

TRACE (board, signed in, focus on UP, Enter held):
1. UP is a plain `<button type=button onClick={guard(() => bet.place("UP"))}>`. It is disabled only by `!stakeReady||insufficient||locallyLocked` (updown-stake-controls.tsx:250-251, 261-262; the comment at :247-249 says pending must not gate it). `guard` only acts on the click event (:149-153).
2. Keydown #1 (repeat=false) bubbles to React's root listener on `document` (Next 16 / React 19.1, package.json:1119,1124). The card wrapper's onKeyDown at updown-card.tsx:994-997 calls `e.stopPropagation()` for Enter and Space. React forwards that to the native event, so no window bubble listener runs. Nothing calls preventDefault, so the keypress fires and the button's activation dispatches a click. `place()` then:
   - passes its gates (use-quick-bet.ts:303-323);
   - mints a fresh idempotency key (:325-327);
   - adds an in-flight entry (:330);
   - starts the action (:332).
   There is no pending or in-flight gate (:163-164 says "do not debounce").
3. Focus stays on UP. The button element persists: only its glyph swaps to a Spinner (:256). No toast or effect moves focus.
4. Every repeat keydown takes the same path. The only consumer of `swallowsHeldKey` in src/ is modal.tsx:291, inside the open-dialog effect (:273-315). With no dialog open, each repeat produces keypress, then click, then another bet. The limits are:
   - `insufficient`, which counts in-flight spend (use-quick-bet.ts:245; stake-math.ts:56-63);
   - the server bucket of 30, refilling 10 a minute (rate-limit.ts:97, checked at market-service.ts:1085).
   Each refusal raises a sticky red toast (use-quick-bet.ts:426). So one held key places up to min(30, balance/stake) bets.
5. When bet 1 resolves, the receipt opens (use-quick-bet.ts:373-377; updown-stake-controls.tsx:347-357). Its primary is onClose (updown-bet-receipt-modal.tsx:125-128; operation-result-modal.tsx:523).
   - Modal records restoreTo=UP (modal.tsx:276-279) and focuses the primary after 30 ms (:282-285, initialFocus at operation-result-modal.tsx:393).
   - Modal listens on the window in the bubble phase (modal.tsx:308). On the board that listener never sees Enter:
     · keys on UP are stopped at `document` by the wrapper;
     · the receipt is portalled into document.body (modal.tsx:416). React's event path crosses the portal into the same wrapper, which stops the native event at body.
   - So a repeat presses "Endelea kucheza" (i18n-dict.ts:3893), onClose runs (use-quick-bet.ts:261), focus returns to UP (modal.tsx:309-314), and the next repeats place more bets. On the board the receipt never stops the burst.
6. Round page with no side chosen (round-stake-panel.tsx:99-107): no wrapper stops Enter. The only onKeyDown handlers in updown are updown-card.tsx:996, updown-stake-controls.tsx:231 and round-stake-panel.tsx:246. Once the receipt's effect runs, held-key.ts:43 swallows every repeat. The burst therefore lasts only for bet 1's round trip. It places no extra bet if the round trip is shorter than the OS repeat delay.
7. Second way in: a first Enter on the receipt's primary (repeat=false, left alone by design, held-key.ts:16,42) closes it. Focus returns to UP, and the held repeats, or a second press, place bets. This is the K/W2 shape.

BROWSER: a held Enter re-presses a focused button on every repeat. A8i says so itself (held-key.ts:4-6). Its own real-browser drive also proved it outside a dialog: in case K the repeats pressed the Sell button that focus had returned to (VODACOM-PLAN.md:1139-1141). Space clicks once, on release, so the finding's Space carve-out is right.

MINOR CORRECTIONS (verdict unchanged):
- The click comes from the keypress's default action.
- On the round page the burst stops when the receipt installs its listener, not when focus moves 30 ms later.
- Before A8i the round page was worse. The removed window listener closed the receipt on every repeat and handed focus back to UP. A8i is a strict improvement there, and the board is unchanged.

- Neither guard covers it (enter-where-pressed.test.mts:32-37; qa-enter-where-pressed.mjs:11-20).

votes.reasoning:
The finding is not refuted. A real browser behaves as it assumes, with only minor nuances. All citations are from the HEAD tree. HEAD has since moved to 7d4b0ad5, but `git diff --stat e6484dd5 HEAD` changes none of the cited files.

BROWSER CHECKS
1. Enter activation. Enter on a focused native <button> clicks it on the keypress that follows each keydown. That holds in Blink, Gecko and WebKit. Every OS auto-repeat keydown produces its own keypress, so a held Enter clicks the focused button on every repeat. Space clicks only once, on keyup, as the finding says.
   - Cancelling a repeat keydown cancels its keypress and its click. That is A8i's own mechanism (modal.tsx:291), and its premise is written at held-key.ts:4-8.
   - Small nuance: activation happens on keypress, not keydown. The effect is the same.
2. Repeat timing. Windows defaults are about a 500 ms delay and about 30 repeats a second, which matches the finding. macOS repeats more slowly. Keyboard events are never coalesced, so a busy main thread delays repeats but does not drop them.
3. Nothing outside a dialog stops a repeat.
   - The only repeat check in src is modal.tsx:291 (a git grep for `.repeat`).
   - No always-on window or document keydown listener handles Enter.
   - useModalLock (src/lib/use-modal-lock.ts:30-77) sets no inert and moves no focus. So UP keeps focus until the receipt's 30 ms move (modal.tsx:282-285), and the receipt records UP as the element to return focus to (modal.tsx:276-279).

CODE CHECKS
- UP and DOWN are disabled only on !stakeReady, insufficient or locallyLocked, never while pending (updown-stake-controls.tsx:251 and :262).
- place() makes a fresh idempotency key on every call (use-quick-bet.ts:325-327) and has no in-flight gate (:302-336).
- The balance check counts in-flight spend (use-quick-bet.ts:245; stake-math.ts:56-63).
- The server allows 30 bets in a burst, refilling 10 a minute (rate-limit.ts:97). A RATE_LIMITED reply shows a sticky red toast (updown-bet-errors.ts:177-178; use-quick-bet.ts:426).
- Next 16.2.4 sends server actions one at a time (node_modules/next/dist/client/components/app-router-instance.js:134-157). Bets already queued still go out after the receipt opens, so this does not lower the count.

ROUND PAGE
- The burst stops when the receipt opens, about 30 ms before it takes focus. From then on the Modal's window listener swallows a repeat Enter aimed at UP (held-key.ts:43).
- For a keyboard player the receipt never closes by itself: it pauses while its focus is :focus-visible (operation-result-modal.tsx:223-229 and :257-262).
- So the extra bets are the repeats that land during bet 1's round trip, after the first 0.5 s.

BOARD
- The card's controls wrapper stops Enter and Space from bubbling (updown-card.tsx:994-997).
- Next hydrates React on `document` (node_modules/next/dist/client/app-index.js:32 and :293).
- The receipt is a React child of that wrapper through its portal (updown-card.tsx:1000-1004, then updown-stake-controls.tsx:347-357).
- So the wrapper stops each native keydown before it reaches the window listener at modal.tsx:308.
- The result is a loop:
  - a repeat presses 'Endelea kucheza', which has no onPrimary, so it just closes (updown-bet-receipt-modal.tsx:110-129; operation-result-modal.tsx:523);
  - the receipt unmounts and focus goes back to UP (modal.tsx:313);
  - the next repeat places a bet.
- It runs until the key is released, the balance runs out or the rate limit refuses.

RECEIPT PATH
- A held Enter on the receipt's primary is real: the repeats after it closes place bets.
- A quick double Enter is also real, but the second press has repeat=false. No held-key rule can stop it. It is the same pattern as W2 in VODACOM-PLAN.md:34-36.

ORIGIN AND SCOPE
- A8i did not introduce this. Before A8i, the success receipt's window Enter listener (4093dc54:operation-result-modal.tsx:373-376) closed the receipt on the next repeat and sent focus back to UP. So the round page already looped for the whole hold.
- A8i limited the round page. The board is unchanged: its wrapper blocked the key both before and after A8i.
- Two of its three ways in are in A8i's own family:
  - the held Enter on the receipt is the money-moving twin of K (VODACOM-PLAN.md:36-37);
  - on the board, A8i's rule never runs at all.
- A8i is already on origin/main (23f762f4 is an ancestor), and the plan already queues this exact item for A8i-2 (VODACOM-PLAN.md:37-38 and :1141-1143). So "in scope" means A8i-2.

REACH
- Only desktop or hardware-keyboard players who hold Enter for 0.5 s or more.
- Safari on macOS does not Tab to buttons by default.
- Every extra bet is real TZS.

2. The repeat guard also closes the held Enter on the receipt: repeats that land on UP after the receipt closes are swallowed.

3. Guard: extend test:enter-where-pressed's census so every money button outside a dialog must carry the repeat guard (or the capture listener must be installed). Add a red plant for it.
4. Drive: add cases to qa-enter-where-pressed. In each, the wallet must move by exactly one stake.
   - Enter held on a board card's UP.
   - Enter held on the round page's UP.
   - Enter held on the receipt's 'Endelea kucheza'.
   - For the round-page case, hold the server action's RESPONSE (route.fetch, wait, fulfill). On localhost the round trip is shorter than any OS repeat delay, so without that the case passes without testing anything.
   - Hold the key the way a real keyboard does: first repeat after about 500 ms, then one every 33 ms. The existing `hold()` repeats after 60 ms (qa-enter-where-pressed.mjs:67-72).
   - Playwright's repeated `keyboard.down` sends repeat=true keydowns plus the keypress, so Chromium does click. A single `press` never repeats.

votes.reasoning:
CONFIRMED. The finding is real and it is money. Note first: the worktree has moved on. HEAD is now cd34231b. A8i went to main as 23f762f4 (origin/main contains it), and src/ and scripts/ are byte-identical to e6484dd5. All citations below are in that tree.

MECHANISM (verified)
- UP and DOWN are onClick-only buttons: updown-stake-controls.tsx:250-251 and :261-262.
- They are disabled only for !stakeReady, insufficient or locallyLocked, never for pending. The comment at :247-249 says so on purpose.
- place() starts a new bet every time it is called, with a fresh idempotency key and no in-flight latch: use-quick-bet.ts:302-336, :325-327, :332. The 'do not debounce' rule is at :163-164.
- The only cap on the client is the balance, and it does count in-flight spend: use-quick-bet.ts:245 and stake-math.ts:56-63. A burst can therefore stake the whole wallet, one chip at a time.
- The server adds a 30-token bucket: rate-limit.ts:97, enforced at market-service.ts:1085-1089. There is no server cooldown and no duplicate check.
- Nothing in src/ reads KeyboardEvent.repeat except modal.tsx:291 (grep). That check runs only while a dialog is open (effect :273-315), as a bubble-phase window listener (:308).
- held-key.ts:4-8 itself states that the browser presses a focused button on every repeated Enter.
- Empirical proof on the A8i tree: hole K (VODACOM-PLAN.md:36 and :1139-1141). A real-Chromium drive showed a held Enter's repeats pressing the Sell button that focus was handed back to. That button is also onClick-only (sell-button.tsx:606, :666). UP is the same kind of button, but nothing stands behind it, so each repeat is a bet.

BOARD CARD (the main surface)
- The wrapper at updown-card.tsx:994-997 calls stopPropagation on Enter and Space.
- The receipt is an OperationResultModal, one of the three dialogs A8i claims to fix. It is portalled to document.body (modal.tsx:319, :416), but it is a React child of that wrapper (updown-stake-controls.tsx:347-357, inside updown-card.tsx:1000-1004).
- So the synthetic keydown reaches the wrapper and stops the native event before it gets to modal.tsx:308. The held-key rule never runs on the board.
- What follows: a repeat presses the receipt's primary (operation-result-modal.tsx:393, :515-523, which calls onClose). Focus goes back to UP (modal.tsx:276-279, :313). The next repeat places another bet.
- The burst is bounded only by the balance, the 30 tokens, the round's lock, or releasing the key.

ROUND PAGE
- There is no such wrapper there; updown-card.tsx:996 is the only onKeyDown in src/ that stops Enter.
- The receipt's Modal swallows repeats once it OPENS, not once it takes focus.
- So the extra bets are the clicks between the OS repeat delay (about 0.5 s) and bet 1's round trip: none on a fast link, many on 2G or 3G.
- Receipt path: holding Enter on 'Endelea kucheza' works like this. The first keydown is not a repeat, so it closes the receipt. Focus returns to UP, and the repeats place bets until the next receipt opens.

CORRECTIONS TO THE FINDING
- The quick double-Enter variant is a deliberate second press (repeat is false). A repeat rule cannot catch it. It belongs to W2's class.
- 'Slow down' refusals stop the money, not the clicking.
- 'Never stops' on the board really means it is bounded by balance, the rate bucket, the lock or the key release.

NOT INTRODUCED BY A8i
- Before A8i, the receipt's own window Enter listener (removed in A8i's operation-result-modal diff) closed the receipt on a repeat and handed focus back to UP. The round page looped; on the board that listener was already starved by the wrapper.
- So A8i strictly improved the round page and left the board unchanged.

NOT A DEFENSIBLE DESIGN CHOICE
- Ali's ruling 'repeat taps are repeat bets' (UPDOWN-UX-AUDIT-HANDOVER.md:213) is about deliberate taps, and it forbids debouncing and disabling while pending.
- Swallowing e.repeat does neither. A long-press on a phone never repeats, so keyboard players would simply match touch players.

NOT GUARDED ELSEWHERE
- No Up & Down case in enter-where-pressed.test.mts:32-37 or qa-enter-where-pressed.mjs:11-20.

SCOPE
- A8i is already live, so 'fix before main' no longer applies. This belongs to A8i-2, where VODACOM-PLAN.md:37-39 and :1142-1143 already queue it pending skeptic confirmation.
- It is in A8i's family because A8i claims 'a key held down from before presses nothing' in the result dialog. On the board that claim is void, and the receipt-close path is hole K with money attached.
- The pure held-on-UP path without a dialog is the same mechanism held-key.ts:4-8 names.

confirmed.title: The board card's Enter/Space stopPropagation (UD-16) stops keys before Modal's bubble-phase window listener, so the held-key rule is dead in the card's receipt and refusal dialogs
confirmed.scenario: On the /updown board, a keyboard player holds Enter on a card's UP, or on the receipt's 'Endelea kucheza'. When a receipt opens, Modal moves focus to 'Endelea kucheza' at +30 ms. The receipt is a React child of the card's controls wrapper, whose onKeyDown calls stopPropagation for Enter and Space. React therefore stops every native repeat at the document root, and Modal's window listener, which holds the held-key rule, never sees it. stopPropagation is not preventDefault, so the repeat still clicks 'Endelea kucheza'. The receipt closes, Modal puts focus back on UP, and the next repeats place bets. The next receipt opens and is pressed the same way. The cycle runs until the key is released or the balance or the bet.place bucket runs out, so the whole balance can go in a few seconds. Keyboard focus also pauses the receipt's 5 s auto-close, so the receipt waits for the next repeat. There are other routes. When a win seal is over an open receipt, Enter held on the seal's Continue closes the seal and focus returns to 'Keep playing'; the next repeat presses it, and the rest are bets. When a held Enter keeps getting refused (for example a cooling-off refusal in UpDownBetBlockedModal), each repeat dismisses the refusal at once, so a refusal that UD-3 says must be read is only glimpsed. On /updown/[roundId] there is no wrapper, so the first receipt to take focus stops the burst. This was the same before A8i, because UD-16 also hid the result modal's old window listener.

- React dispatches at the container that matches the target (:19273-19316). Its listener walk then climbs instance.return through the portal into the wrapper (:19420-19441).
- React's stopPropagation calls the native one (:3394-3401).

2. Why the repeat still presses the button
- stopPropagation does not cancel the default action. In Chrome and Safari, Enter presses a focused button through the keypress default (a simulated click), and every auto-repeat keydown produces its own keypress unless the keydown was cancelled. Firefox behaves the same way.
- Repeats go to whatever has focus after a script moves it, with repeat=true. A8i's own drive case C, red on the old tree, relies on exactly this.
- Playwright's CDP autoRepeat sets KeyboardEvent.repeat just like a real OS repeat, and the wrapper stops both the same way. A drive would therefore reproduce this.

- The receipt passes no onPrimary (updown-bet-receipt-modal.tsx:110-129), so its primary just closes it (operation-result-modal.tsx:515-523). The receipt then unmounts (:69).
- Modal's cleanup puts focus back on the element saved when it opened, which is UP (modal.tsx:276-279, :309-314). The page is not made inert: use-modal-lock only sets overflow.
- UP stays enabled while a bet is in flight (updown-stake-controls.tsx:247-251). place() has no in-flight guard and makes a new idempotency key on every click (use-quick-bet.ts:302-337). Each repeat that lands on UP is a new real bet.

- Space is not a route here: it presses on keyup, so a held Space bets once, on release.

- On the round page, once a receipt is open, the rule swallows every Enter repeat on the page, including during re-keys. But two things still bet on both surfaces, outside any dialog:

confirmed.title: The dial ignores e.repeat: a held Enter across a BUSY reply reopens the confirm with a new key under 'Retry now'
confirmed.scenario: A keyboard player opens the bet confirm from the dial (Enter on role=slider), then presses and holds Enter on Confirm. The repeats are swallowed while the bet is pending. The server answers BUSY or system_error, which is retryable. The confirm closes and Modal returns focus to the dial. The failure result opens, but it takes focus only at +30 ms. A repeat that lands on the dial in that window runs the dial's React onKeyDown before Modal's window listener sees it. Once pending has fallen, openConfirm() mints a NEW idempotency key and reopens the confirm, and the confirm's later 30 ms timer wins focus. If the confirm reopens within its 140 ms exit beat, it keeps its earlier portal node, so the failure dialog (same z 100, later node) paints over it. On release, the player sees 'Retry now' while focus sits on the covered Confirm. Enter then calls submit() with the new key instead of retrySubmit's same key. If the first attempt had in fact landed (system_error means the outcome is unknown), that is a second bet. If the reopen comes after the beat, the player instead faces a bet confirm they never asked for.

confirmed.title: Enter in the withdraw amount box submits the withdrawal with no confirm
confirmed.scenario: An approved player on /wallet/withdraw, with payouts open, clicks or Tabs into Amount, types 20000 and presses Enter (or the Go/arrow key on an Android numeric keypad). The form has exactly one text field and no submit button, so the browser submits it implicitly (HTML implicit submission). React runs withdrawAction(formData), which calls withdraw() and redirects to /wallet?withdrawal=…&status=…. The money leaves for the registered number without the 'Confirm withdrawal' dialog ever opening. The player never sees the amount, the tax/fee row, the 'You receive' net or the recipient name, so a mistyped amount goes out without review. Repeated Enters are deduplicated by the form's single idempotency key, so this is one withdrawal, not several.
confirmed.evidence: src/app/wallet/withdraw/page.tsx:222-225 (<form action={withdrawAction}>, no onSubmit), :226 (hidden key), :227-232 (radio inputs, which do not block implicit submission), :236-247 (AmountField), :285 (hidden msisdn), :295 (WithdrawConfirm is the only control when canSubmit). src/components/wallet/amount-field.tsx:52-67 has the only text input; its chips are type=button (:76-80). src/components/ui/input.tsx:506, :606 and :652 render it as type='text', and :574-576 do not preventDefault Enter. The trigger is type=button (src/app/wallet/withdraw/withdraw-confirm.tsx:205-212), and ConfirmDialog forces type button (src/components/ui/confirm-dialog.tsx:131-141), so the form has no submit button. The intended path is submitForm, then requestSubmit after the dialog (withdraw-confirm.tsx:136-150); the dialog shows the disclosure at :174-191. src/app/wallet/withdraw/actions.ts:54-124 moves the money. By contrast, the deposit form is safe only because it has more than one text field: the amount, the tel msisdn (src/app/wallet/deposit/page.tsx:245-256) and six always-mounted billing inputs (src/components/wallet/card-billing-fields.tsx:53-58, :67-111). The codebase already relies on 'a disabled submit button stops an implicit submission' (src/components/ui/modal.tsx:660-662).
confirmed.proposedFix: Block implicit submission on the withdraw form and route Enter to the confirm. In the amount box, handle Enter with preventDefault and run the same openGuard/onOpen/setOpen path that the trigger runs. Alternatively, put a disabled default submit button first in the form (<button type='submit' disabled hidden aria-hidden tabIndex={-1} />), which per the HTML spec stops implicit submission outright. Apply the same to the deposit form, so it does not depend on its field count, and to every <form action> whose commit sits behind ConfirmDialog. Add a QA case: type an amount on /wallet/withdraw and press Enter; the confirm must open and the balance must be unchanged.

1. Block implicit submission natively, so it holds even before hydration. Make the first submit button in the withdraw form a disabled default button: `<button type="submit" disabled hidden aria-hidden="true" tabIndex={-1} />`. A disabled default button stops implicit submission outright; modal.tsx:660-662 already relies on that. `form.requestSubmit()` at withdraw-confirm.tsx:149 submits from the form itself, so the real confirm path is unaffected. Make it a kit primitive and place it in every `<form action>` whose commit sits behind ConfirmDialog (25 files use ConfirmDialog). The close-account phrase box is the other known live case. Add it to deposit too, which is safe today only because of its field count.

2. Then make Enter open the confirm. Give AmountField an `onEnter`. On a first-press Enter (`!e.repeat`), call preventDefault and run the trigger's own path: openGuard, then onOpen, then setOpen(true). That can be `buttonRef.current?.click()` in WithdrawConfirm, or an imperative open() on ConfirmDialog. The dialog then opens on Cancel (modal.tsx:626), and A8i's held-key rule swallows the repeats (modal.tsx:291). Do NOT make the trigger type=submit: before hydration, a tap would POST straight to withdrawAction.

3. Add a guard and a drive.

   - qa case: on /wallet/withdraw, type 20000 and press Enter. The 'Confirm withdrawal' alertdialog must be visible, no server-action POST may go out, and the balance must be unchanged. Repeat with Cancel, and again for the close-account phrase box.

votes.reasoning:
Confirmed. Real browsers behave the way the finding says. I checked at worktree HEAD 7d4b0ad5, which equals origin/main and has a clean tree. A8i landed there as 23f762f4. No wallet, withdraw or confirm-dialog file differs between 4093dc54, e6484dd5 and HEAD.

1) THE RULE AND THE FORM. Under the HTML spec, a form with no submit button and exactly one field that blocks implicit submission (text, tel, number and similar) is submitted when Enter is pressed in that field. Blink (SubmitImplicitly), Gecko (ImplicitSubmissionIsDisabled) and WebKit all count text fields this way. The withdraw form (src/app/wallet/withdraw/page.tsx:222-296) holds:
- exactly one text field: the amount box, which the Input atom renders as type=text (src/components/ui/input.tsx:606, :652; src/components/wallet/amount-field.tsx:52-67);
- hidden inputs (page.tsx:226 -> idempotency-key-field.tsx:19; page.tsx:285);
- radios (provider-radio-grid.tsx:65-77);
- buttons that are all type=button: the chips (amount-field.tsx:76-80) and the trigger (withdraw-confirm.tsx:206-208), whose type is forced by confirm-dialog.tsx:131-132.
The dialog's own submit button is not mounted while the dialog is closed (modal.tsx:317), and when open it is portaled to document.body (modal.tsx:319, :416). So the withdraw form never has a default button.

2) NOTHING CANCELS ENTER. The submit is the default action of the Enter keypress. The Input's keydown handler only records the key and calls no preventDefault (input.tsx:574-576). The window keydown listeners present on the page act only on Escape or arrow keys (install-invite.tsx:174-178, channels-panel.tsx:302-306, first-visit-primer.tsx:321-328), and scroll-cast.tsx:130 is passive.

3) VALIDATION PASSES. The radios are required, but the first rail is checked by default (provider-radio-grid.tsx:45, :74, :76). The amount box has no required or pattern, and its min/max do nothing on a text input (input.tsx:604-606).

4) THE ACTION RUNS. React 19.2.5 runs a function form action on any native submit that has no submitter and was not prevented (node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-client.production.js:12136-12196). So withdrawAction(formData) runs (actions.ts:54-124). It never checks that the confirm was used: it checks the bounds (:102-104), calls withdraw() (:115-119) and redirects (:124).

5) ANDROID. Chrome sets the keyboard's action key to Go when the form has no later text field (buttons do not count). Pressing Go, or any action other than Next or Previous, makes Chrome send a synthetic Enter keydown and keypress, so the form submits the same way. iPhone's inputmode=numeric number pad has no return key, so iOS users reach this only with a hardware keyboard. That narrows who is affected; it does not refute the finding.

6) FIREFOX ALSO SUBMITS FROM A RADIO. Gecko's Enter-on-radio path calls MaybeSubmitForm, so Enter on a provider tile probably submits too (not driven). Chrome does not do this.

7) HELD ENTER AND PLAYWRIGHT. A held Enter auto-repeats keypress and submits again. The duplicates are deduplicated: the key comes from a stable useRef (idempotency-key-field.tsx:18-19), withdraw() checks it (wallet-service.ts:1561-1567), and Transaction.idempotencyKey is @unique (prisma/schema.prisma:684). So it stays one withdrawal, as the finding says. Playwright's keyboard.press('Enter') sends text "\r", which produces the same keypress, so a drive reproduces this faithfully.

8) ROOT CAUSE. Commit 27e17d38 (E-215, 2026-08-25) replaced the form's second text field, the tel msisdn Input, with a hidden input. That second field had been blocking implicit submission. The defect has been live since then.

9) HARM. A mistyped amount (up to TZS 5,000,000) leaves without the review the dialog exists for: amount, fee, net and recipient (withdraw-confirm.tsx:3-7, :174-191; confirm-dialog.tsx:4-8). The fee is charged on it: 1.5% by default (market-config.ts:220), up to 5% (:619), computed at payout.ts:583-585. The destination is pinned to the player's registered number (page.tsx:68-85), which limits the loss to the player's own money and fee, with no stranger paid.

10) THE DEPOSIT CONTRAST IS ACCURATE. The deposit form has the tel number field (deposit/page.tsx:245-256) and six billing Inputs inside a wrapper hidden only by CSS (card-billing-fields.tsx:57, :67-117). Those still count, so the form has two or more blocking fields and Enter does not submit it.

SCOPE. This is not A8i's family. No dialog acts and no held key from before is involved: the confirm never opens. The repo already files this as A8j, "reported, pre-existing, money", "outside the family" (docs/VODACOM-PLAN.md:39-41, :1145-1146).
votes.fixAdvice:
Fix this as A8j, soon, because it is live for every player. Do not rely only on the "disabled default submit button" rule. The spec, Blink and Gecko honour it. WebKit's submitImplicitly, however, has historically skipped a disabled or display:none submit button and still submitted a form with one text field, so check this in Safari before relying on it. ConfirmModal's hard tier is safe either way, because its onSubmit re-checks `armed` (modal.tsx:665-672).

A gate that works in every browser:
1. In WithdrawConfirm, mark sends from the dialog with a ref, set in submitForm just before requestSubmit (withdraw-confirm.tsx:136-150).
2. Add a native 'submit' listener on buttonRef.current.closest('form'), or make the form a client component with onSubmit. It calls preventDefault on every submit the ref did not mark. React then skips the action (react-dom-client.production.js:12163-12179).
3. On a refused submit, take the trigger's path (guardOpen, then onOpen, then open; buttonRef.current.click() is enough). Do it only on a fresh press, never on a repeat. The dialog opens on Cancel (modal.tsx:626), and Modal already swallows held-key repeats (modal.tsx:291).
4. Optionally, also call preventDefault on a non-composing Enter keydown in AmountField.

This one gate also covers the Android Go key and Firefox's Enter on a radio tile. Apply the same gate to:
- the close-account phrase form (the other half of A8j);
- every other <form action> whose commit sits behind ConfirmDialog;
- the deposit form, so its safety stops depending on how many fields it has.

Add a guard and a qa drive. On /wallet/withdraw, type 20000 and press Enter, hold Enter, and press Enter on a provider tile. Each time the confirm must open on Cancel, no server-action POST may be sent, and the balance must stay the same. Run it in Chromium and Firefox, and in WebKit if one is available.

confirmed.scenario: A keyboard player presses Enter on the dial and then, impatiently, presses Enter again 80-150 ms later. People do this when a page seems slow, and it also happens with a keyboard that double-types or a bouncing key. The second keydown is not a repeat. In Chromium a focused <button> turns an Enter keypress into a click. Because it is a click, React 19 flushes the re-render in a microtask, long before any second Enter or key repeat.

2. **React keeps the focused node and relabels it "Yes".**
   - Both branches return a host <span> with no key (idle :71, confirm :49), so React keeps the root.
   - Children are matched by index:
     - idle is [Button Retry, Button Cancel] (:72, :75);
     - confirmCancel is [span, Button Yes, Button No] (:50-52).
   - Index 0 changes type (Button to span), so the Retry node is deleted.
   - Index 1 is the same type, Button, so React reuses its fiber.
   - Button is one forwardRef that always renders a single <button> (button.tsx:65-70). Only its icon and text children change (:84-86).
   - The focused DOM node is never removed or moved. React's own selection restore keeps focus on the earlier focused element while it stays in the document.

3. **Nothing on this page swallows the next Enter.**
   - A8i's held-key rule lives only in Modal's effect. It returns when the Modal is not open (modal.tsx:273-274) and installs its listener only while open (:291, :308). This inline confirm is not a Modal.
   - The only other keydown listeners on admin pages handle Escape only: ai-toolkit.tsx:55 and admin-mobile-nav.tsx:39.
   - Nothing between the button and the root handles keys: there is no onKeyDown on the row, ScrollX (scroll-x.tsx:31-48) or the table.

4. **Consequence.**
   - The action passes the officer's normal gate: role plus session 2FA (payment-actions.ts:33-36, rbac-guard.ts:185).

confirmed.title: The rewritten sell-button note says two fast clicks share the same-tick window, which React 19 rules out
confirmed.scenario: A reader of sell-button.tsx concludes that a fast double click on the Sell confirm can reach submit twice before pending lands. Under React 19, the first click's pending state commits before the second click's task runs, and a disabled button receives no click. Only a second call within the same task (a script, or two synthetic .click() calls) falls in that window.
confirmed.evidence: sell-button.tsx:339-341: 'a double press from any surface (two fast clicks, a script) is the same window'. useTransition sets isPending through an optimistic update on SyncLane, which commits in the microtask after the event, so the button is disabled={pending || quoteExpired} (sell-confirm-modal.tsx:161) before the next click. The inFlight latch (sell-button.tsx:345 and :388-389) is still correct.
confirmed.proposedFix: Change the wording to 'a second call in the same task (a script or a synthetic double .click())'. Keep both latches.

votes.reasoning:
I could not refute it. The finding holds: the comment is wrong about "two fast clicks", and the code is right.

Note on HEAD: the worktree has moved from e6484dd5 to 7d4b0ad5, and that commit is also origin/main. A8i is already on main as 23f762f4. `git diff e6484dd5 HEAD` is empty for sell-button.tsx, sell-confirm-modal.tsx and modal.tsx, so every line number below holds at both commits. `git blame` puts the comment (sell-button.tsx:336-344) in the A8i commit 66e6b61c. The claim appears nowhere else in the repo, and origin/main still has it at sell-button.tsx:340.

What happens when a real player double-clicks Sell (React is the build Next ships, 19.3.0-canary-3f0b9e61, react-dom-client.production.js:18263):
1. First click: the Sell button's onClick (sell-confirm-modal.tsx:160) calls `submit` (sell-button.tsx:543). That sets `inFlight.current = true` (:389) and calls `start(async ...)` (:393).
2. `startTransition` (react-dom-client.production.js:5447) sends `isPending = true` as an optimistic update on lane 2, the SyncLane (:5643-5663).
3. That schedules a microtask to process the root (:11865-11891, :13229-13237, :13409-13417). The click handler (`dispatchDiscreteEvent`, :17476-17492) does not render anything synchronously.
4. When the click handler returns, the browser runs its microtasks before any other task. `processRootScheduleInMicrotask` then renders and commits the sync update (:13287-13311).
5. That commit gives the Sell button `disabled={pending || quoteExpired}` (sell-confirm-modal.tsx:161). The prop reaches it unchanged: `pending` passes in at sell-button.tsx:539, and Modal draws `{children}` in a plain portal with no memo (modal.tsx:319-400).
6. Second click: it is a separate input task, so it arrives after that commit and finds a disabled button. The browser does not send a click to a disabled button. React also refuses: its `getListener` drops onClick on a disabled `button` (:1627-1657).

So no real double click or double tap can call `submit` twice. Enter is no exception. It is the same click on the focused button, and the comment's own sentence at :339-340 says React re-renders after it, which contradicts "two fast clicks" one line later.

Only a second call made before the first click's handler returns gets past the `pending` check, for example a script calling `.click()` twice in a row. `inFlight` (:345, :388-389, reset at :469) catches that, so both latches are correct.

One small correction to the finding: "the same task" is a little loose. A second `.click()` after an `await` in the same task already finds the button disabled, because React queued its microtask first.

Severity is docs: the code behaves correctly, and only the reasoning a maintainer reads around this money control is wrong. It is in scope for A8i because A8i introduced the wording.

Only a second call made before the first press's handler returns falls in that window, for example a script calling .click() twice in a row or calling `submit` directly. `inFlight` is set SYNCHRONOUSLY on the first call, so it is the only latch that closes that window."

The finding is correct. Only the comment is wrong; the code is fine.

1. A8i added the sentence. It does not exist at 4093dc54 and is new in 4093dc54..e6484dd5. The text is the same at HEAD 7d4b0ad5 (sell-button.tsx:339-341) and in A8i's squash commit 23f762f4. So the sentence was literally true then, and that literal truth was the defect A8i fixed. A8i added select.tsx:288-289: `if (at !== document.body && !triggerRef.current?.contains(at) && !listRef.current?.contains(at)) return;`. Since then the listener ignores keys whose target is outside the body, the trigger and the list. Read on its own, line 269 now says more than the code does.

In that block, "every key" means keys that arrive while focus is on the trigger (262-263: "Focus stays on this trigger ... so every key reached this handler AND the list's window listener"). A key aimed at the trigger still passes line 289, because Node.contains counts the node itself. The opening key is still stopped at 274-275. So "contradicts" overstates it. "Broader than the code" is accurate.
(2) The new scope is written 15 lines below, at the listener itself (284-287). It is also in DESIGN_AUTHORITY.md section A8 point 8 ("The kit Select's open list takes only keys pressed in it or on the page itself").
(3) DESIGN-BASELINE.md:72 says only "one trigger handler, one window listener", which is accurate.
